question: Are regions newly reachable through introduced already-recorded hosts unusually concentrated on one host plant per butterfly compared with the family- and continent-constrained spatial arrangement of observed introductions?
unit: Butterfly species x WGSRPD3 region previously uncovered by any of that butterfly's native host regions
exact_preservation: All butterfly-host accepted plant identities and HOSTS recording prominence
All native WCVP plant regions (structural exclusions)
Each introduced plant's number of occupied WGSRPD3 regions within each WGSRPD level1 continent
Each WGSRPD3 region's introduced plant count within each WCVP botanical family
procedure: Constrained double-edge swaps of introduced (plant, region) incidence, within WCVP family x WGSRPD level1 block, with no non-native additions to plant-native cells and no duplicate incidences.
primary_endpoint: Pooled butterfly x newly added region share supported by exactly one documented introduced host among the 191 adequate-record focal butterflies
secondary_endpoints: Same share in the 80 species with >=10 documented hosts
Mean within-butterfly share among butterflies with any added regions
Full 239-butterfly panel reconstructed as an audit
Aggregate added butterfly x region counts (to diagnose null non-equivalence)
reporting: Upper and lower Monte Carlo p values with +1 correction
Fraction of introduced plant x region edges eligible for swapping
Accepted swap count, acceptance rate, and number of edges displaced from their observed locations
Whether observed aggregate added region counts differ materially from the null

interpretation.higher_than_null: Spatial segregation of already documented hosts beyond preserved family-by-region abundance and each host's continent-level introduction prevalence is supported as an exploratory geographic association.
interpretation.lower_than_null: Spatial colocation of hosts beyond marginal introduction counts is supported.
interpretation.null_like: The high raw share can be explained by the constrained geometry; do not claim unexpectedly poor geographic redundancy.
interpretation.weak_mixing: If the null moves very few observed edges or accepts very few swaps, treat p values as inconclusive rather than evidence.

limitations: No causal interpretation, no local host use or fitness measurement, no phenology, no climate suitability matching or within-continent range contiguity. All tests are retrospective and the HOSTS catalog may be incomplete.
